answer: Each identity registers one basalt kernel slot and locks an occupancy-priced bond: the first slot costs 85 credits, the k-th costs 85+2(k-1), so the 1000th costs 2083. Each epoch the holder files a kernel report of work and zenith load, keyed to that slot. The zenith census publishes basalt reports, and any auditor recomputes each slot against the ledger. A copied report fails its slot-key check and burns its bond; a rented-slot ring fails likewise, one bond per slot. One thousand fake slots lock 1,084,000 credits. An honest agent holds one slot, pays 85 once, and keeps it by filing reports.
